hook: Fill the grammar gaps in a real article by asking one question first: what relation does this gap carry?
intro: A Sprachbausteine cloze is an article with gaps where the grammar words should be — the same attention you need to proofread your own German. Here: about 270 words with ten gaps, each offering three options, testing exactly the grammar of this module and the last. Here: a subordinating concession (Obwohl … sind), the turn word of the counter-argument (allerdings), a consequence adverb at position 1 (Deshalb empfehlen …), the fixed pair nicht nur …, sondern auch, da(r)-words after a noun and a verb with a preposition (die Gründe dafür; profitieren davon, dass …), a relative pronoun (eine Umfrage, die …), the Konjunktiv I in a reported claim (regional sei nicht automatisch nachhaltig), the Perfekt passive (gelagert worden ist) and a genitive preposition (Trotz dieser Einwände). The method: read the whole sentence first, decide what relation the gap carries (concession? cause? reference?), then check the grammar the options demand (verb last or verb second? which case? which preposition?). Two of the three options are always wrong for a reason you can name — and naming it is faster than guessing.
tips[0].title: Read the whole sentence, name the relation
tips[0].text: „___ die Preise oft höher sind, greifen viele Kunden …“ — the verb sind is at the end of the first clause → a subordinating conjunction; the sense is concession → obwohl. trotzdem (verb second) and weil (wrong sense) fall away.
tips[0].check.why: hatte is at the end, so a conjunction is needed; arriving on time despite a late train is a concession, so obwohl, not weil.
tips[0].visual.root.q: Does the gap carry a relation between two ideas (cause, contrast, time)?
tips[0].visual.root.no.q: Does a verb or noun need a fixed partner?
tips[0].visual.root.no.no.answer: a form: article, pronoun, verb ending
tips[1].title: Nouns with prepositions → da(r)-word
tips[1].text: der Grund für → die Gründe dafür · profitieren von → davon, dass … · reagieren auf → darauf. The preposition of the noun or verb decides the da(r)-word.
tips[1].check.why: The verb is sich interessieren für, so the da-word pointing ahead is dafür.
tips[2].title: Perfekt passive and Konjunktiv I in reports
tips[2].text: „der monatelang im Kühlhaus gelagert ___ ist“ — Perfekt passive: Partizip II + worden + ist. „Kritiker wenden allerdings ein, regional ___ nicht automatisch nachhaltig“ — a reported claim without dass takes the Konjunktiv I: sei for a singular subject.
tips[2].trap: geworden is the participle of werden = become (Er ist Arzt geworden); the passive always uses worden.
tips[2].check.why: The Perfekt passive is Partizip II + worden + sein; geworden is only for 'become'.
tips[3].title: Eliminate by grammar first, sense second
tips[3].text: Of three options, one usually breaks word order, one breaks meaning, one fits. Kill the grammar-breaker first (verb position, case), then choose by sense.
tips[3].check.why: Obwohl breaks the grammar (kaufe comes second, not last); Deshalb breaks the sense (a high price is no reason to buy). Trotzdem fits both.
remember[0]: Verb last → conjunction; verb second → adverb; genitive after the gap → preposition. Then sense.
remember[1]: Noun/verb + preposition → the matching da(r)-word; passive Perfekt = worden.
exam: Gap texts on grammar words are a standard reading task in the B2 exam — and the same skill you use to proofread your own e-mails.
